name: Question 15
problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $B(-7,12,-3)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨-7,2,4⟩+s⟨-5,3,1⟩$ and $r=⟨-22,17,13⟩+t⟨1,5,6⟩.$
worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨-5,3,1⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨1,5,6⟩$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $B(-7,12,-3)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $b=⟨-7,12,-3⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =b+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨-7,12,-3⟩+s⟨-5,3,1⟩+t⟨1,5,6⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point B(−7,12,−3) and is parallel to the lines r=⟨−7,2,4⟩+s⟨−5,3,1⟩ and r=⟨−22,17,13⟩+t⟨1,5,6⟩.

a
r=⟨−7,−3,12⟩+s⟨−3,4,2⟩+t⟨1,5,5⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=⟨−7,−3,12⟩+s⟨3,3,1⟩+t⟨1,5,7⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=⟨−7,12,−3⟩+s⟨−3,5,1⟩+t⟨1,6,5⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=⟨−3,12,−7⟩+s⟨1,3,−5⟩+t⟨1,6,5⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=⟨−7,12,−3⟩+s⟨−5,3,1⟩+t⟨1,5,6⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The direction vectors of the lines are v1=⟨−5,3,1⟩ and v2=⟨1,5,6⟩, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point B(−7,12,−3) lies on the plane and its position vector is b=⟨−7,12,−3⟩.

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

r=b+sv1+tv2r=⟨−7,12,−3⟩+s⟨−5,3,1⟩+t⟨1,5,6⟩,s,t∈(−∞,∞).
